items.name: Builder
items.summary: A builder for a regex based on a hybrid NFA/DFA.

methods.summary: Build a regex from the given pattern.

methods.name: build_from_dfas
methods.signature: fn build_from_dfas(&self, forward: DFA, reverse: DFA) -> Regex
methods.summary: Build a regex from its component forward and reverse hybrid NFA/DFAs.

methods.name: build_many
methods.signature: fn build_many<P: AsRef<str>>(&self, patterns: &[P]) -> Result<Regex, BuildError>
methods.summary: Build a regex from the given patterns.

methods.name: dfa
methods.signature: fn dfa(&mut self, config: dfa::Config) -> &mut Builder
methods.summary: Set the lazy DFA compilation configuration for this builder using [`dfa::Config`].

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Create a new regex builder with the default configuration.

methods.name: syntax
methods.signature: fn syntax(&mut self, config: util::syntax::Config) -> &mut Builder

items.name: Cache
items.summary: A cache represents a partially computed forward and reverse DFA.

methods.name: as_parts
methods.summary: Return references to the forward and reverse caches, respectively.

methods.name: as_parts_mut
methods.summary: Return mutable references to the forward and reverse caches, respectively.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Return a reference to the forward cache.

methods.name: forward_mut
methods.summary: Return a mutable reference to the forward cache.

methods.name: memory_usage
methods.summary: Returns the heap memory usage, in bytes, as a sum of the forward and reverse lazy DFA caches.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Create a new cache for the given `Regex`.

methods.name: reset
methods.summary: Reset this cache such that it can be used for searching with the given `Regex` (and only that `Regex`).

methods.name: reverse
methods.summary: Return a reference to the reverse cache.

methods.name: reverse_mut
methods.summary: Return a mutable reference to the reverse cache.

items.name: FindMatches
items.summary: An iterator over all non-overlapping matches for an infallible search.

items.name: Regex
items.summary: A regular expression that uses hybrid NFA/DFAs (also called "lazy DFAs") for searching.

methods.name: builder
methods.summary: Return a builder for configuring the construction of a `Regex`.

methods.name: create_cache
methods.summary: Create a new cache for this `Regex`.

methods.name: find
methods.signature: fn find<'h, I: Into<Input<'h>>>(&self, cache: &mut Cache, input: I) -> Option<Match>
methods.summary: Returns the start and end offset of the leftmost match. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: find_iter
methods.signature: fn find_iter<'r, 'c, 'h, I: Into<Input<'h>>>(&'r self, cache: &'c mut Cache, input: I) -> FindMatches<'r, 'c, 'h>
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over all non-overlapping leftmost matches in the given bytes. If no match exists, then the iterator yields no elements.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Return the underlying lazy DFA responsible for forward matching.

methods.name: is_match
methods.signature: fn is_match<'h, I: Into<Input<'h>>>(&self, cache: &mut Cache, input: I) -> bool
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this regex matches the given haystack.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Parse the given regular expression using the default configuration and return the corresponding regex.

methods.name: new_many
methods.summary: Like `new`, but parses multiple patterns into a single "multi regex." This similarly uses the default regex configuration.

methods.name: pattern_len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of patterns matched by this regex.

methods.name: reset_cache
methods.summary: Reset the given cache such that it can be used for searching with the this `Regex` (and only this `Regex`).

methods.name: reverse
methods.summary: Return the underlying lazy DFA responsible for reverse matching.

methods.name: try_search
methods.signature: fn try_search(&self, cache: &mut Cache, input: &Input<'_>) -> Result<Option<Match>, MatchError>
methods.summary: Returns the start and end offset of the leftmost match. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.
